title: Bulk report - Week 41
summary:
Capesize
The market remained under pressure through the week, with persistent Atlantic weakness outweighing a gradual recovery in the Pacific. The 5TC continued to edge lower, falling from $43,833 on Monday to $39,363 by Friday. The Pacific showed greater resilience as fixing activity gathered pace, with close to 20 vessels reported on Wednesday alone.

children.title: Capesize
children.summary: The market remained under pressure through the week, with persistent Atlantic weakness outweighing a gradual recovery in the Pacific. The 5TC continued to edge lower, falling from $43,833 on Monday to $39,363 by Friday.

children.title: Panamax-Kamsarmax
children.summary: Market conditions improved steadily over the week following a quiet and cautious start. The P5TC edged lower early on before recovering those losses and ending the week higher overall.

children.title: Ultramax/Supramax
children.summary: Activity in the Atlantic slowed, but rates only softened slightly, from the Continent scrap numbers were still very strong with a 63,000-dwt fixed delivery Tyne for scrap to the East Mediterranean at $38,000. In the US Gulf fronthaul rates dipped below transatlantic levels during the week, but the highlight earlier in the week was a 64,000-dwt fixed for coal to India at $38,000 basis a minimum guaranteed duration of 60 days.

children.title: Handysize
children.summary: The Handysize market ended the week on a mixed but broadly steady footing, with regional trends continuing to shape sentiment. The Continent and Mediterranean remained broadly balanced, with rates generally holding near last-done levels despite pockets of fresh demand.
